questions.note: Stature, head size and torso length match the drawing well. The shoulders read square and high with no trapezius slope, the upper arms are smooth even tubes, and the narrow waist and tight trouser seat make the hips read slimmer than the reference. The legs are long by declaration.

The wide stance, the turned-out right foot and the carbine's diagonal from right chest to left thigh match closely in the onion. Departures: arms hang squarer from the shoulders, the left hand sits about 70 px high, the right pauldron sticks out like a fin, and the head is upright and more frontal than the reference's slight turn and tilt.

Every listed item exists and sits roughly where drawn: gaiter, carrier, shingles, antenna at left rear, pauldrons, forearm guards, belt pouches, thigh rigs, knee pads, boots. Size and form miss: the upper-arm plate is short, the right forearm guard sits at the elbow, the elbow pad is a disc, the knee pads are pillows, the right thigh pouches are oversized boxes, and the emblem is wrong.

The order of the layers is right and nothing obviously passes through, but several plates stand off instead of resting: the right pauldron floats like a fin, the left shoulder plates are flat cards, strap pads poke up at the neck, a rear belt item juts out, and the left hand lies on the handguard without closing. The trousers cling like skin at the seat and crotch.

The man's lean V-taper is close, but the kit is thinner than drawn. The carrier is a flat slab without the bulky placard and tall pouches, the shoulder and forearm armour are thin bands instead of thick plates, the trousers are tight above the knee and the boots are slim. Only the thigh mag pouches are bulkier than the reference.

The right hand on the pistol grip, index finger straight along the receiver, reads as the reference, and the stock tucked under the right arm against the chest is right. The left hand lies on top of the handguard with its fingers hanging down the far side instead of cupping it from below and wrapping over, so the gun looks balanced rather than gripped.

defects.what: Pauldrons, arm bands and forearm guards are near-black with a white salt-and-pepper speckle, like chipped black paint; the reference's armour is worn tan/olive with blue-grey steel faces and soft brown wear.
defects.fix: Base the plates on the reference's olive-tan polymer with blue-grey steel face plates; wear as edge abrasion and brown grime, not white flecks.

defects.what: The right pauldron is a flat plate standing off the top of the shoulder like a fin, with a second flat card below it; it neither wraps the deltoid nor rests on it.
defects.fix: A real shoulder guard is a curved cap shaped to the deltoid, strapped flush, with the upper-arm plate hinged below it.

defects.what: On the left arm the reference's long upper-arm plate, running from the shoulder cap almost to the elbow, is replaced by a short square plate and a strap band; the outer upper arm shows bare sleeve.
defects.fix: One tall curved plate on the outer upper arm from under the shoulder cap to about 60 mm above the elbow, held by two straps.

defects.what: The right forearm guard is a short cuff sitting at the elbow; the forearm below is covered by a long smooth glove gauntlet, where the reference has a segmented guard from below the elbow to the wrist.
defects.fix: Move the guard down to span mid-forearm to wrist, segmented plates over a strap base, with the glove cuff ending under it.

defects.what: The left elbow pad is a thin disc on the point of the elbow; the reference shows a thick hard elbow cap that stands well proud of the sleeve.
defects.fix: A moulded elbow cup about 20 mm thick over the olecranon, strapped round the arm.

defects.what: The emblem on the left pauldron is a pale star on a grey panel; the reference shows a crossed-blade X mark on a dark blue-grey shield-shaped panel.
defects.fix: Reproduce the reference's X/crossed-blade mark and the shield outline and colour of its panel.

defects.what: The knee pads are rounded black pillows with tan flecks; the reference's pads are angular hexagonal hard caps with a raised tan/olive frame round a dark faceted plate.
defects.fix: AirFlex-class pad: faceted hard cap with a raised rim, tan/olive frame and dark centre, buckled strap at the side.

defects.what: The trousers read mid-grey with pale camo blotches and grow lighter toward the cuffs; the reference's trousers are dark charcoal-brown with muddy tan patches.
defects.fix: Darker charcoal base with brown-tan mud staining concentrated at the knees and shins, no pale grey wash.

defects.what: The right thigh rig is two oversized flat black boxes with slots, wider and squarer than the reference's slimmer worn holster and magazine pouches.
defects.fix: Narrower kydex-style mag carriers sized to a STANAG magazine, with the reference's worn tan/olive edge wear.

defects.what: The left hand lies on top of the handguard with its fingers hanging down the far side; it does not close round the handguard as the reference's supporting hand does.
defects.fix: Palm under and beside the handguard, fingers curled up over its far side, thumb along the near side.

defects.what: The right boot reads as a smooth galosh: a plain upper with no toe cap or panels above a high flat rand; the reference boot has a scuffed rubber toe cap, stitched leather panels and a chunky lugged sole.
defects.fix: Zephyr-class boot: separate toe bumper, suede/nylon panels with stitch lines, distinct midsole and lug outsole.

defects.what: The carrier front is a plain flat light grey-khaki slab with three short open shingles; the reference is olive-brown with a laser-cut placard, admin panel and tall flapped pouches.
defects.fix: Olive-brown worn Cordura, a raised placard with its panel and three tall flapped magazine pouches reaching toward the belt.

defects.what: The hair is a solid dark cap with a jagged top edge and a hard painted hairline; the reference has short textured mid-brown hair with volume swept up on top and faded sides.
defects.fix: Strand or card hair, longer and lifted on top, short taper at the sides, mid-brown.

defects.what: The trousers are skin-tight at the crotch and seat like leggings; the reference's combat trousers hang loose with folds above the knee.
defects.fix: Crye G3-class cut: roomy seat and thighs, gusseted crotch, folds where the fabric hangs.

defects.what: The pad at the top of the right shoulder strap pokes up beside the neck as a flat card corner instead of lying over the shoulder.
defects.fix: Strap pads drape over the trapezius and follow it down front and back.

defects.what: An L-shaped item on the rear right of the belt projects well behind the hip and does not appear to rest on the belt.
defects.fix: Seat the item flat against the belt with its loop round the belt.

defects.what: The gloves are smooth rubbery mitts with sausage fingers and long gauntlet cuffs; the reference's gloves are M-Pact-class with knuckle armour, padded panels and a short cuff.
defects.fix: Short-cuff mechanic-style glove with a moulded knuckle guard, finger panels and a wrist strap.

defects.what: The carbine is a flat even dark grey with no wear on the edges and no tan accents; the reference's carbine is gunmetal with tan anodised parts and worn edges.
defects.fix: Black/gunmetal anodised finish with lighter worn edges and the reference's tan accents on the stock and receiver.

defects.what: The shoulder line is square and high, nearly level from neck to deltoid; the reference's shoulders slope down from a visible trapezius.
defects.fix: Lower and round the shoulder tops so the line falls from the neck to the deltoid.

ranked: [D1] The armour reads as black metal with white paint chips everywhere; the reference's plates are worn tan/olive with blue-grey steel faces. This one colour choice changes the whole figure's identity.
[D12] The carrier is a plain pale khaki slab. The reference's carrier, the centrepiece, is olive-brown, busy and bulky, with a placard and tall flapped pouches.
[D2] The right pauldron sticks out like a fin off the shoulder instead of capping it. It breaks the silhouette and looks unattached.
[D3] [D4] The arm armour is in the wrong places and sizes: the left upper-arm plate is short, and the right forearm guard sits at the elbow with the forearm bare under a long glove.
[D10] The left hand rests on the handguard instead of gripping it, so the hold looks posed rather than carried.
[D7] The knee pads are soft black pillows; the reference's are faceted hard caps with tan frames.
[D8] The trousers are grey-washed and get lighter toward the cuffs; the reference's are dark charcoal with brown mud.
[D14] The trousers cling at the crotch and seat like leggings. Combat trousers hang loose there.
[D11] The boots read as smooth galoshes, with no toe cap, panels or stitching, in flat grey.
[D17] The gloves are smooth rubber with long gauntlets; the reference's have knuckle armour and short cuffs.
[D13] The hair is a hard cap with a jagged top. With the declared parametric face it makes him read as a younger, rounder, different man and weakens every judgement of the whole figure.
[D9] The right thigh mag pouches are oversized boxes, and their black plastic is too clean against the reference's worn kit.
[D19] The shoulders are square and high with no trapezius slope, which reads mannequin-like next to the reference's sloped shoulders.
[D6] The left shoulder emblem is a star; the reference's is a crossed-blade X on a shield.
The shirt sleeves are perfectly smooth tubes with no seams or folds, so the arms read inflated rather than clothed.
[D18] The carbine is one flat dark grey, missing the reference's tan accents and edge wear.
[D5] The left elbow pad is a thin disc where the reference has a thick cap.
[D15] [D16] Small pieces stand off what holds them: a strap pad corner beside the neck, and an L-shaped item jutting from the rear belt.
